function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content: Electricity wasn’t “discovered” by a single person—it emerged from the work of many scientists over centuries.  Early observations of static electricity date back to ancient Greeks like Thales of Miletus, who noted that rubbing amber produced attraction.  In the 17th and 18th centuries, figures such as William Gilbert (who coined the term *electricus*), Otto von Guericke, and later Benjamin Franklin (whose famous kite experiment in 1752 helped demonstrate the electrical nature of lightning) made foundational contributions.  By the 19th century, scientists like Alessandro Volta, Michael Faraday, and James Clerk Maxwell built on these discoveries to develop the modern understanding of electricity and electromagnetism.
